prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor doorway layout with a close wall carrying a wireframe graphic on the left (about 0.5–1.5 m away, within arm's reach of the camera wearer), a central doorframe pillar (about 1.5–2 m away), and a recessed room on the right containing a white armchair (~3–4 m away) and distant background furnishings (~4–6 m away, rendered nearly black). A seated person in the lower center-right foreground is roughly 1–1.5 m in front of and below the camera wearer's viewpoint—within or just at the edge of arm's reach—with a white chair back immediately behind their left shoulder and their lower body occluded by the bottom frame edge. Across the five frames, the camera view shifts closer to the left wall and blurs in frames 3 and 5, while in frame 5 the foreground person stands up and approaches to within 0.5–1 m on the right, extending their right arm into the foreground and looking slightly upward toward the camera wearer's right rather than looking down and to the right as in frames 1–4. Compared to the RGB strip alone, the depth map clarifies the sharp step in distance between the foreground doorway wall and the recessed room beyond, as well as the continuous 3D silhouette of the approaching person's torso and right hand in the heavily motion-blurred fifth frame. However, the map is unreliable across frames 1, 3, and 5: in frame 1 the person's head blends almost completely into the wall depth behind them, and in the motion-blurred frames 3 and 5 the left foreground wall flips from bright (near) to dark (falsely far) due to scale and blur artifacts.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates key foreground and background regions across the scene: the wireframe graphic on the close left wall (0.5–1.5 m away, within the camera wearer's reach), the person in the lower-center foreground (~1–1.5 m away in frames 1–4, approaching to <1 m on the right in frame 5), the white armchair (~3–4 m away, ~2 m behind the person to the right), and small potted plants/lamps (~4–5 m away above and behind the armchair). In frames 1–4, the person's head and upper shoulders are located below eye level between the left wall graphic and the right-side armchair, facing downward and slightly right away from the camera wearer with their body below the shoulders cropped out of the bottom of the frame; in frame 5, the person rises into the right half of the frame, facing more forward and slightly right while their right hand reaches within arm's reach of the camera wearer and the white chair behind them. The segmentation masks make it easier than in the motion-blurred RGB frames (especially frames 3 and 5) to see the outer contour of the person's torso, head, and extended right arm separated from the dark clothing and blurred background. However, the map is highly unreliable in its semantic class labels and temporal consistency: it misclassifies the 2D wall graphic as a 'bird' (frames 1, 2, 4) or 'cat' (frame 3), relabels the person's hair in frame 4 as a 'dog', switches the white armchair label between 'bed', 'couch', and 'chair' before missing it entirely in frames 3 and 5, and fails to segment the white chair directly behind the person.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only small, crumpled yellow body-skeleton clusters near the bottom edge of frames 1, 2, and 4 (at the location of the seated person's head, roughly 1–1.5 m in front of and below the camera wearer), while frames 3 and 5 are completely black with no detected keypoints and no magenta hand skeletons appear in any frame. From the RGB context, the person is seated in frames 1–4 facing downward and slightly right (not looking at the camera wearer) with their arms and torso occluded below the bottom frame boundary, and then stands up and moves closer (<1 m) on the right in frame 5 with their right arm and hand reaching out within arm's reach of both the chair back and the camera wearer. Because the pose detector collapses all full-body keypoints onto the visible top of the person's head in frames 1, 2, and 4, it provides only a rough 2D localization of the head's horizontal position near the lower border and adds almost no true skeletal structure beyond what is visible in RGB. The map is severely unreliable throughout the sequence, hallucinating a compressed full-body skeleton inside the hair region when the torso and limbs are out of view and completely failing to detect the person's upright upper body, head orientation, or extended right hand during the motion-blurred frames 3 and 5.
